§3§lAn optional remote input§r
Matrix Grouped Item/Fluid Input Mirrors (ME) let a remote machine use an ordinary source group. §1Mirrors share the source's real inventory§r, with no extra buffer or external ME connection. Ordinary groups work without mirrors. Keep source and destination loaded in the §1same dimension§r.

§3§lMatch the layout§r
Match the source's member count, item/fluid types and relative positions. At the destination, replace §1one§r corresponding member with a same-kind mirror; all other members remain ordinary. Only one mirror is allowed per destination group. The complete layout may rotate horizontally. Keep destination inventories and pattern slots empty, with no external ME entry.

§3§lBind with a native GT Data Stick§r
With the source buffer empty and all processing finished, left-click an ordinary source member with the Data Stick, then right-click the destination mirror. §1The copied member and mirror must match in position and item/fluid kind§r; any position can be used. For four item positions A/B/B/C, copying position 2 means placing the item mirror at destination position 2; the two B positions remain distinct. Check the success message and source address in the group interface.

§3§lOne shared stock§r
Patterns and incoming materials stay at the source. All consumers draw from that stock; mirrors neither copy materials nor add a separate processing inventory. Before rebinding, empty the source and finish all processing. Understand the mapping and binding steps, then tick this quest.
